_what: Files whose slash-separated date order the data itself cannot prove, and
the order this project has decided to parse them with.
`pipeline/sql/15_dates.sql` derives the order per file from evidence: a
first field above 12 can only be a day, a second field above 12 can only
be a month. A file that shows neither is 'ambiguous' and a file that shows
both is 'conflict'. Day-first and month-first agree for every date with
day <= 12, so about 40% of an ambiguous file's rows parse 'successfully'
under the wrong convention with day and month transposed — a June trip
quietly becoming a December one, with nothing to surface it.
The pipeline used to default those to month-first and print a line. This
file replaces the default: an ambiguous or conflicting file must be named
here, with the evidence for the order chosen, or extraction's clean stage
ABORTS with etl.AmbiguousDateOrder. A NEW ambiguous file is exactly the
case a default is worst for — nobody looks at a line that has printed on
every run for a year.
Entries are checked both ways. A file listed here that the data can now
resolve on its own raises etl.StaleDateOrderException, so the list cannot
quietly outlive the ambiguity it documents.
THE LIST IS EMPTY, and that is a finding rather than an oversight. The one
file this mechanism was written for — van-mobi 2025-05 — turned out not to
be ambiguous at all. It is 'YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS': 133,643 slashed rows,
one distinct first field ('2025'), one distinct second field ('05'), third
fields spanning 01..31. Both evidence regexes in 15_dates.sql capture one
or two digits before a slash, so a four-digit year matched neither, both
counts came out zero, and the file was labelled ambiguous and parsed by the
month-first fallback. It parsed correctly, for the wrong reason, and the
runbook, the clean-stage log and the warehouse all reported an ambiguity
the file does not have. The fix is `year_evidence` in 15_dates.sql, not an
entry here — a declaration saying 'month' would have recorded something
false about a file that is year-first, and this file's own stale-entry
check refused it when it was tried.
So what ships is the mechanism and no exceptions. An empty list here means
every file in the archive proves its own date order from its own values,
which is the state to want.

_schema.date_order: 'day' or 'month' — the order the file's dates are written in
